sources.title: Gemma 4 31B IT model card
sources.evidence: Identifies the instruction-tuned Gemma 4 31B checkpoint, Apache-2.0 license, text/image inputs and text output, configurable thinking and native function calling. Its video example explicitly loads google/gemma-4-31B-it. Fresh October 27 read also confirms base_model: google/gemma-4-31B; no count transfer from an unrelated family or derivative is needed.

sources.title: Gemma 4 31B IT configuration
sources.evidence: Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration: 60-layer dense text decoder, hidden size 5376, MLP width 21504, vocabulary 262144, 262144 positions, tied word embeddings, 50 sliding and 10 full-attention layers. Includes a 27-layer vision encoder; audio_config is null. Reopened on October 27: same pinned configuration; no weight payload fetched.

sources.title: Gemma 4 31B IT tensor index
sources.evidence: Maps 1188 tensors to two BF16 shards. total_size is 62546177752 bytes. metadata.total_parameters is 32682372656, which exceeds the Transformers parameter-only count (31,273,086,512) by exactly the tied 1409286144-element token embedding; it is not the unique full-model total. Reopened on October 27: 1188 entries, two shards and both metadata values unchanged; the earlier header census was not repeated.

sources.title: Gemma 4 31B IT first safetensors header
sources.evidence: Read only bytes 0-7 and 8-136903 via HTTP 206 Range requests. The 136896-byte JSON header contains 1009 tensors; combined with shard 2, every indexed tensor occurs exactly once. No weight payload downloaded.

sources.title: Gemma 4 31B IT second safetensors header
sources.evidence: Read only bytes 0-7 and 8-23591 via HTTP 206 Range requests. The 23584-byte JSON header contains 179 tensors. Both headers sum to 31273088876 BF16 elements: text 30697345340, vision tower 569550384, vision projection 6193152.

sources.title: Gemma 4 Transformers implementation
sources.evidence: Ties lm_head.weight to model.language_model.embed_tokens.weight. Registers vision std_bias/std_scale as feature-standardization buffers (1152 each) and layer_scalar as a buffer. Remaining indexed matrix, embedding and norm weights are model parameters; no quantization scale tensors occur in this BF16 checkpoint.

sources.title: Google Gemma 4 transformer blocks
sources.evidence: Block creates skip_scale with self.param and multiplies the complete layer output by it. The corresponding 60 layer scalars are stored in the Flax params collection, unlike the buffer classification in Transformers; this alone does not establish their optimization history.

sources.title: Gemma 4 checkpoint conversion
sources.evidence: Explicitly maps Google skip_scale to layer_scalar and vision standardization bias/scale to std_bias/std_scale, connecting the original model parameters with the checkpoint names.

sources.title: Gemma 4 Technical Report
sources.evidence: July 2026 report confirms decoder-only Transformers, dense 31B, and separate approximate counts: 1410M embedder, 29290M einsums, 550M vision encoder and 500M optional drafter. The 30.7B text figure is not the complete multimodal checkpoint. Does not give a separate active count for 31B. Reopened on October 27 alongside the current developer model card; this absence of a Google active figure does not negate the independently attributed nominal benchmark convention in s17.

sources.title: Gemma 4 launch announcement
sources.evidence: Dated April 2, 2026; announces release of 31B Dense and links directly to the exact google/gemma-4-31B-it checkpoint. Announces available BF16 weights, Apache 2.0, video/image processing, reasoning and function calling.

sources.title: Gemma 4 31B IT repository history
sources.evidence: The earliest returned commit is 419b2efe421994fdfd3394e621983d4cc511cd4f, dated 2026-04-02T10:52:51Z and titled Preparing for release!; this exact variant corroborates the April 2 launch. Repository creation on March 11 does not establish public availability.

sources.title: Gemma release chronology
sources.evidence: Current chronology says March 31, 2026 for Gemma 4 31B and other initial sizes. This conflicts with the contemporaneous April 2 launch linking the exact IT checkpoint and its April 2 release-preparation commit; the chronology alone does not establish an earlier public release for this variant.

sources.title: Gemma 4 model card
sources.evidence: 31B column reports dense, 60 layers, 30.7B, 256K context, text/image and no audio, with approximately 550M vision encoder separately. Family supports configurable thinking and native function calling.

sources.title: Gemma 4 multi-token prediction documentation
sources.evidence: Lists google/gemma-4-31B-it among target models and constructs its separate -assistant checkpoint name. MTP requires loading a second model; no drafter tensors belong to the inspected target checkpoint.

sources.title: Gemma 4 31B IT processor configuration
sources.evidence: Contains Gemma4VideoProcessor with frame sampling as well as Gemma4ImageProcessor, corroborating exact-model video support. Shared audio preprocessing metadata does not override the absent audio model and explicit no-audio model card.

sources.title: Google Gemma 4 vision standardization
sources.evidence: Standardize applies (x - bias) * scale. Google represents these arrays in the Flax params collection; Transformers distinguishes them as standardization buffers. These 2304 values are separated in the accounting; their learning history is not independently established.

sources.title: Alem: Benchmarking Open-Ended Multi-Agent Coordination in Language Agents, Figure 11 and Table 1
sources.publisher: Kale-ab Abebe Tessera et al. (University of Edinburgh, University of Oxford and University College London)
sources.evidence: Original June 6, 2026 research paper. Table 1 identifies gemma-4-31b-it among the evaluated models. Figure 11 plots its Gemma 4 31B point at approximately 31 billion on an axis explicitly labeled Active parameters (billions, log scale). The original PDF page 24 was visually inspected; this is the authors' nominal comparison convention, not a Google disclosure or a component-resolved count of every parameter used on each generated token.

sources.title: Alem original PDF, page 24 active-parameter plot
sources.evidence: Figure 11 visually distinguishes Gemma 4 31B at approximately 31B active from Gemma 4 26B/A4B and E4B near 4B. Nominal plot precision is retained; no exact value is reverse-engineered from pixels. The same paper's Table 1 disambiguates the plotted 31B model as the instruction-tuned variant.

sources.title: Gemma 4 on AI Gateway
sources.evidence: April 2, 2026 original provider announcement explicitly names google/gemma-4-31b-it and states that all parameters of its 31B Dense model are active during inference. Corroborates the nominal dense inference convention but does not resolve vision-prefill versus text-decode participation or establish the precise 31.2731B full checkpoint as an active count.

sources.title: Introducing Gemma 4 models on Amazon Bedrock
sources.evidence: June 15, 2026 original serving announcement identifies instruction-tuned Gemma 4 31B with 30.7B in a combined Total / Active parameters row. Because that cell does not separately distinguish total from active, it corroborates the published text-model size but is not used to assert a more precise active count.

sources.title: The Gemma-4 experiment: one model for chat, OCR and reranking
sources.evidence: August 24, 2026 original deployment experiment labels 31B dense as 30.7B Active params/token. Not used to establish precision: the adjacent bandwidth explanation divides 260 GB/s by 15.4 GB yet claims about 7 tokens/s, and uses a four-bit-ish assumption while the table labels the configuration BF16. It does not expose a component-resolved active census or link the named underlying benchmark report.

sources.title: A Visual Guide to Gemma 4
sources.evidence: Reopened the developer visual guide, originally published by its Google DeepMind author. It explicitly identifies the 31B dense variant and its separate vision encoder, but its numeric active-count discussion concerns 26B A4B. Dense architecture alone is not the basis for the active value recorded here.

name.note: Exact google/gemma-4-31B-it instruction-tuned variant; 31B is its nominal size label.

developer.note: Google DeepMind is the author; retain the catalog developer normalization Google.

family.note: Gemma 4 belongs to the Gemma model family.

release_date.note: Retain April 2: contemporaneous launch explicitly links this IT checkpoint and its earliest release-preparation commit is April 2. Current family chronology says March 31; recorded as a source conflict rather than treating repository creation or a later chronology as proof of earlier public availability.

open_weights.note: Official complete BF16 target checkpoint is publicly accessible.

license.note: Exact checkpoint card declares apache-2.0; launch confirms Apache 2.0.

parameters_b.note: Complete unique target-model count rounded to 0.0001B, robust to small scalar/buffer classification differences. Header elements: 31,273,088,876 = text 30,697,345,340 + vision tower 569,550,384 + projection 6,193,152. Transformers classifies 60 block scalars and 2,304 vision standardization values as buffers, leaving 31,273,086,512 nn.Parameter elements. Google stores corresponding scalars/standardization arrays in Flax params; their optimization history is not established, so no exact learned count is asserted. Both conventions round to 31.2731B. Tied token embedding/output head counted once. Index total_parameters exceeds the Transformers parameter-only count by the 1,409,286,144-element tied table; total_size/2 agrees with headers. Includes the complete vision component. Separate optional MTP assistant excluded. The official 30.7B text figure omits the vision component. October 27 re-audit reopened the pinned card, configuration and index plus current Google documentation and the original technical report; no supported change to the complete total was found. Named-base searches resolve to google/gemma-4-31B; no pruning, distillation or resizing was established for this IT record. Previous header accounting is retained without downloading weights or repeating the census.

active_parameters_b.note: Approximately 31B under the active-model-size convention used by Tessera et al. in the original Alem research paper, Figure 11; Table 1 identifies gemma-4-31b-it. The plot was visually checked in the PDF on page 24. Vercel independently identifies the exact IT model and explicitly describes all parameters of its nominal 31B Dense variant as active during inference. This is an attributed nominal benchmark convention, not a separately published Google per-token measurement and not the precise 31.2731B full checkpoint total. No component scope is assigned because the plot does not decompose text, vision, embeddings or inference phases. Fresh exact-model total/active/component and named-base searches also checked later primary material: Google's report/card and visual guide give no distinct 31B active figure; AWS's combined Total / Active cell is ambiguous; Certant's 30.7B active table has inconsistent neighboring bandwidth arithmetic and precision assumptions. Unsupported aggregator active figures are not used. Exact modality-dependent participation remains unresolved.

architecture.note: Dense decoder-only text Transformer with 60 layers (5 local to 1 global attention), tied embeddings and a separate vision Transformer encoder plus projection; not MoE.

context_window.note: Exact text max_position_embeddings; model card rounds this to 256K.

modalities.note: Exact 31B IT video example and video processor establish video input via sampled image frames. No native audio model: audio_config is null and card says No Audio.

reasoning.note: Configurable thinking mode is explicitly documented for instruction-tuned Gemma 4, including the 31B model.

tool_call.note: Native function calling is a source-reported capability; no local inference test is claimed.

description.value: Instruction-tuned dense Gemma 4 model for text generation from text, images and video, with configurable thinking and function calling.
description.note: Plain description of the exact IT model without performance superlatives.

patch.description: Instruction-tuned dense Gemma 4 model for text generation from text, images and video, with configurable thinking and function calling.

sources.label: Alem research paper: nominal active-model-size comparison

patch.notes: Full unique multimodal target checkpoint is approximately 31.2731B parameters; Google's 30.7B figure covers the text backbone. Active ~31B follows the nominal comparison convention in Tessera et al.'s Alem paper, not a Google measurement of modality-specific participation. Tied output/token embedding counted once; optional separate MTP assistant excluded. Video is processed as image frames; no native audio. Retain April 2, 2026 for the exact IT public launch; current family chronology instead lists March 31.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains the supported ~31.2731B unique multimodal target total after reopening pinned metadata and original Google sources, without repeating the tensor census or downloading weights. Recovers a nominal ~31B active count from Tessera et al.'s original Alem Figure 11, with the exact IT identity established in Table 1 and corroboration from Vercel's explicit dense-inference statement. This is the research authors' approximate comparison convention, not a Google per-token disclosure or a component-resolved count. Exact modality-dependent activity remains unresolved. All non-parameter assessments, including video without audio and the April 2 versus March 31 release-date conflict, are preserved.
